# Judith Chapter 7 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 7

---

## Council Notes

**Key decisions for this chapter:**

- **v. 4 — "lick-clean the face" (Greek: *ekleixousin*):** EMET preserves the vivid Greek idiom "lick clean." LOGOS and PNEUMA replace with "devour" and "strip bare." SOPHIA sides with a middle path: "they will devour the whole face of the land" — keeping "face of the land" from the Greek while smoothing the verb.
- **v. 18 — geographic names:** All three translators preserve the place names. SOPHIA follows their lead but aligns on LOGOS's ordering.
- **v. 22 — "their children were dispirited":** EMET's "dispirited" translates *oligopsychei* most precisely. LOGOS renders "dispirited" as well. PNEUMA's "went limp" is vivid but loses the soul-language. SOPHIA keeps "dispirited."
- **v. 28 — "we call to witness" formula:** EMET's "we-call-to-witness against you" is the most literal. LOGOS and PNEUMA both paraphrase. SOPHIA preserves the legal-witness formula.
- **v. 30 — "five days" ultimatum:** All three translators agree on the structure. The theological weight — putting God on a deadline — is preserved without commentary.

---

**7:1** The following day Holofernes ordered his entire army and all his allied forces to march against Bethulia, seize the passes into the hill country, and make war on the Israelites.

**7:2** Every able-bodied man broke camp that day. Their combined forces numbered one hundred and seventy thousand infantry and twelve thousand cavalry, not counting the supply train and the additional foot soldiers — an exceedingly great multitude.

**7:3** They encamped in the valley near Bethulia, beside the spring, spreading out as far as Dothaim in breadth and from Bethulia to Cyamon in length — Cyamon being the place that faces Esdraelon.

**7:4** When the Israelites saw their vast numbers, they were deeply dismayed and said to one another, "These men will devour the whole face of the land; neither the high mountains nor the valleys nor the hills can bear the weight of their forces."

**7:5** Each man took up his weapons, they lit signal fires on their towers, and they stood watch throughout that night.

**7:6** On the second day Holofernes led out all his cavalry before the Israelites at Bethulia,

**7:7** reconnoitered the approaches to their city, found the water sources, seized them, and posted armed guards over them, then returned to his troops.

**7:8** Then all the chieftains of the Edomites, all the leaders of the Moabites, and the commanders of the coastal peoples came to him and said:

**7:9** "Let our lord hear a word from us, so that his army does not suffer a defeat.

**7:10** For these Israelites do not rely on their spears but on the height of the mountains where they live; it is no easy matter to scale the peaks of their mountains.

**7:11** Therefore, lord, do not engage them in open battle — not one man of your force needs to fall.

**7:12** Stay in your camp, keeping every man of your army secure, and send your servants to hold the spring that flows from the foot of the mountain —

**7:13** for that is where all the inhabitants of Bethulia get their water. Thirst will destroy them and they will surrender the city. Meanwhile, we and our troops will ascend the summits of the nearby mountains and camp there, keeping watch to ensure not one man leaves the city.

**7:14** They will waste away — they and their wives and their children — and before the sword ever touches them they will be laid out dead in the streets where they live.

**7:15** And you will repay them with evil for their rebellion, for refusing to receive you in peace."

**7:16** These words pleased Holofernes and all his attendants, and he ordered that it be done as they had proposed.

**7:17** The Ammonite contingent moved out along with five thousand Assyrians; they encamped in the valley and seized the waters and water sources of the Israelites.

**7:18** The Edomites and Ammonites went up and encamped in the hill country opposite Dothan; they sent some of their men toward the south and east, toward Egrebel, near Chous by the stream of Mochmur. The rest of the Assyrian army spread out across the plain and covered the entire face of the land; their tents and baggage train formed a vast encampment — a very great multitude.

**7:19** The Israelites cried out to the Lord their God, for their spirits sank; all their enemies had encircled them and there was no way of escape.

**7:20** The whole Assyrian army remained encamped around them — infantry, chariots, and cavalry — for thirty-four days, until every water vessel belonging to all the inhabitants of Bethulia was exhausted,

**7:21** the cisterns were running dry, and they did not have enough water to drink even for a single day; it was being rationed out by measure.

**7:22** The children were dispirited; the women and young men were collapsing from thirst, falling in the streets of the city and at the passages of the gates, until there was no strength left in any of them.

**7:23** Then all the people gathered against Uzziah and the leaders of the city — the young men, the women, and the children — and cried out with a loud voice before all the elders:

**7:24** "May God judge between us and you! For you have done us great harm in not seeking peace with the Assyrians.

**7:25** And now there is no one to help us. God has sold us into their hands to be laid prostrate before them in thirst and utter ruin.

**7:26** So now summon them and surrender the whole city as plunder to the forces of Holofernes and his entire army.

**7:27** It is better for us to become their plunder. We will be slaves, but our lives will be spared, and we will not have to watch our infants die before our eyes or see our wives and children perish.

**7:28** We call to witness against you heaven and earth and our God and the Lord of our ancestors — who punishes us for our sins and the sins of our ancestors — that he should not bring this thing to pass today."

**7:29** There was loud and bitter weeping from the whole assembly, and they cried out to the Lord God with a great voice.

**7:30** And Uzziah said to them: "Take courage, brothers — hold out five more days, during which the Lord our God may turn his mercy toward us, for he will not abandon us completely.

**7:31** But if those days pass and no help comes, I will do as you have said."

**7:32** He dismissed the people, each to his post, and they went off to the walls and towers of the city. The women and children he sent to their houses. And the city was brought very low in distress.
